title: Quasi-coherent algebras and invariant sections on a flat affine action quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $H$ an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $E$ a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra with a rational $H$-action. Here rational means a $k$-algebra coaction $\rho_E:E\to E\otimes_k k[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, and $E^H=\{e:\rho_E(e)=e\otimes1\}$. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^H)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathcal X=[U/H]$ be the fppf quotient stack of torsors with equivariant maps to $U$, and let $\pi:U\to\mathcal X$ and $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be its presentation and invariant morphism [lem-sfb-flat-affine-action-stack-presentation]. Pullback along $\pi$, followed by affine sections, gives an equivalence between quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebras and commutative $E$-algebras $D$ endowed with a rational $H$-coaction extending that on $E$. Quasi-coherence on a stack is tested on smooth charts as in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. This equivalence identifies surjections with surjective equivariant $E$-algebra maps. For every corresponding pair $\mathcal D,D$, there is a natural isomorphism $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal D)\cong D^H$, where $D^H=\{d:\rho_D(d)=d\otimes1\}$. For $\mathcal D=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ this identifies the map $E^H\to\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$ induced by $\phi$ with the identity of $E^H$. There is no finite-generation restriction on $D$.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), applied to the affine action groupoid; groupoids.tex Section equivariant (definition-equivariant-module). Algebra objects and their sections are obtained compatibly with multiplication and the unit.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-flat-affine-action-stack-presentation] for the algebraic stack $\mathcal X$, its presentation $\pi$ and the invariant morphism $\phi$, with its convention: $b:U\times_kH\to U$ is dual to $\rho_E$, $h\cdot x=b(x,h^{-1})$, and torsors use left translation. Set $C=k[H]$, $L=E\otimes_kC$, $x*h=b(x,h)$, and $R=U\times_kH$ with $s(x,h)=x*h$, $t(x,h)=x$, $e(x)=(x,1)$, $i(x,h)=(x*h,h^{-1})$ and $c((x,h),(x*h,g))=(x,hg)$; thus $s^\sharp=\rho_E$, $t^\sharp(e)=e\otimes1$, and $e^\sharp,c^\sharp$ are dual to $\epsilon,\Delta$. Send $(x,h)\in R(T)$ to the element $h$, an arrow $x*h\to x$ of the action groupoid of [lem-sfb-affine-group-torsor-stackification] with $G=H$, $V=U$ and $a(h,u)=h\cdot u$, because $h\cdot(x*h)=x$. This is a bijection on arrows compatible with source, target, identity and inverse, and with composition: for $a=(x,h)$ and $b=(x*h,g)$ the composite $a\circ b:x*(hg)\to x$ is the element $hg$, since $h\cdot(g\cdot y)=(hg)\cdot y$. Hence the group and action identities give the laws of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws], and the fppf stackification $[U/R]$ of the prestack with objects $U(T)$ and arrows $R(T)$ is the stackification $\mathcal A$ of that lemma. That lemma gives $\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal T$, sending $x$ to the trivial torsor $(H_T,h\mapsto h\cdot x)$ and $(x,h)$ to right translation $g\mapsto gh^{-1}$; check: $(gh^{-1})\cdot x=g\cdot(x*h)$. Here $\mathcal T$ is literally the stack $\mathcal X$ of the presentation lemma, and the trivial torsor over $U$ is $\pi$. So the canonical object $a:U\to[U/R]$ goes to $\pi$ and restriction along $a$ is pullback along $\pi$. No flatness of $s,t$ is needed below.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks) in Situation 04WL, as stated in the cited torsor stackification; with the presentation of the cited lemma

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-descent-tensor-cokernel] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ to this groupoid; it assumes no flatness or finiteness. Its quasi-coherent modules are those of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. It gives an equivalence, full and faithful on all compatible maps, with pairs $(\mathcal M,\delta:s^*\mathcal M\simeq t^*\mathcal M)$, $e^*\delta=1$, $c^*\delta=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\delta\circ\mathrm{pr}_2^*\delta$, sending $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ to $\mathcal O_U$ with its canonical datum and tensor products to tensor products with the tensor datum. As $U,R$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules and their maps with $E$-modules $M$ and $E$-linear maps; [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identifies sections of $s^*\widetilde M,t^*\widetilde M$ naturally with $M\otimes_{E,s^\sharp}L$, $M\otimes_{E,t^\sharp}L$; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] identifies sections of $\widetilde M\otimes\widetilde N$ with $M\otimes_EN$. So $\delta$ is an $L$-linear isomorphism with $\delta_e=1$, $\delta_a\delta_b=\delta_{c(a,b)}$. An algebra structure on a descended module is then equivalent to compatible maps $M\otimes_EM\to M$ and $E\to M$: fullness descends them, and faithfulness on their tensor-power sources verifies associativity, commutativity and the unit equations; pullback carries those equations back. Fullness and faithfulness applied to the product and unit composites of a compatible algebra map give the assertion on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent) as stated in the cited module descent; affine coordinates schemes.tex Tags 01IB, 01I9, 01I8

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization] with $C=k[H]$ to the underlying $E$-module $D$. It identifies the identity and cocycle datum with a counital coassociative semilinear map $\rho_D:D\to D\otimes_k C$. Under its tensor formula, compatibility of the multiplication map is exactly
$\rho_D(dd')=\rho_D(d)\rho_D(d')$.
Compatibility of $j:E\to D$ is exactly $\rho_D(j(e))=(j\otimes1)\rho_E(e)$, including $\rho_D(1)=1\otimes1$. Thus these are precisely $k$-algebra coactions extending $\rho_E$, in both directions. The morphism criterion in that lemma identifies algebra maps commuting with the datum with equivariant algebra maps. This proves the requested equivalence, with no smoothness assumption.

source.place: Tag 06WT, affine calculation; groupoids.tex Tag 03LF (definition-equivariant-module); Hopf identities dual to the group laws

proof.text: An algebra map $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ is a surjection in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] exactly when every section lifts locally, i.e. when the module-sheaf cokernel of its underlying module map is zero. By the cokernel clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-descent-tensor-cokernel] this cokernel corresponds to the cokernel of $\widetilde D\to\widetilde{D'}$ on $U$, whose affine sections are $D'/u(D)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](3). An equivalence sends exactly the zero objects to zero objects, and a quasi-coherent module on $U$ is zero iff its affine sections are. So $u$ is a surjection iff $D\to D'$ is surjective, in both directions.

source.place: Tag 06WV and 06WT, cokernels computed on the presentation

proof.text: By [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], a global section $z$ gives an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-linear map $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal D$, $a\mapsto az$; evaluation at $1$ is its inverse. Full faithfulness and the unit clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-descent-tensor-cokernel], with [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], identify these with $E$-linear maps $f:E\to D$ compatible with the data, where $E$ carries $\rho_E$ by the unit clause of [lem-sfb-hopf-coaction-linearization]. Such $f$ is $e\mapsto j(e)d$ with $d=f(1)$. By the morphism criterion of that lemma, compatibility is $\rho_D(j(e)d)=(f\otimes1)\rho_E(e)$; at $e=1$ this says $\rho_D(d)=d\otimes1$, and that equality implies it for every $e$, since $\rho_D(j(e)d)=\rho_E(e)(d\otimes1)=\sum j(e_{(0)})d\otimes e_{(1)}$. Thus restriction gives exactly $D^H$. Addition, multiplication and the unit are preserved because restriction of algebra sections preserves them. An equivariant algebra map sends $d$ to its image, proving naturality.

source.place: Tag 06WT, full faithfulness applied to maps from the structure module

proof.text: For $\mathcal D=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$, pullback and affine sections give $(E,\rho_E)$, so the preceding isomorphism is restriction into $E$ with image $E^H$. By step 1 restriction to $U$ is pullback along $\pi$, and the presentation lemma says that $\phi\pi$ is induced by $E^H\hookrightarrow E$. Consequently the composite $E^H\to\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})\to E^H$ sends each $e$ to $e$. The module equivalence and all displayed tensor formulas apply to arbitrary modules and algebras, so no finite generation of $D$ is required.
